In [[probability theory]], the '''Skorokhod problem''' is the problem of solving a [[stochastic differential equation]] with a reflecting boundary condition.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Lions | first1 = P. L. | last2 = Sznitman | first2 = A. S. | author2-link = Alain-Sol Sznitman| doi = 10.1002/cpa.3160370408 | title = Stochastic differential equations with reflecting boundary conditions | journal = Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics | volume = 37 | issue = 4 | pages = 511 | year = 1984 }}</ref>

The problem is named after [[Anatoliy Skorokhod]] who first published the solution to a stochastic differential equation for a [[reflecting Brownian motion]].<ref>{{cite journal | first = A. V. | last = Skorokhod | author-link = Anatoliy Skorokhod | title = Stochastic equations for diffusion processes in a bounded region 1 | journal = Theor. Veroyatnost. I Primenen. | volume = 6 | year = 1961 | pages = 264–274}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | first = A. V. | last = Skorokhod | author-link = Anatoliy Skorokhod | title = Stochastic equations for diffusion processes in a bounded region 2 | journal = Theor. Veroyatnost. I Primenen. | volume = 7 | year = 1962 | pages = 3–23}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | title = Stochastic differential equations with reflecting boundary condition in convex regions | first = Hiroshi | last = Tanaka | journal = Hiroshima Math. J. | volume = 9 | issue = 1 | year = 1979 | pages = 163–177 | doi = 10.32917/hmj/1206135203 | url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.hmj/1206135203| doi-access = free }}</ref>

==Problem statement==

The classic version of the problem states<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1007/s11134-010-9187-9| title = Pathwise comparison results for stochastic fluid networks| journal = [[Queueing Systems]]| volume = 66| issue = 2| pages = 155| year = 2010| last1 = Haddad | first1 = J. P. | last2 = Mazumdar | first2 = R. R. | last3 = Piera | first3 = F. J. }}</ref> that given a [[càdlàg]] process {''X''(''t''), t&nbsp;≥&nbsp;0} and an [[M-matrix]] ''R'', then stochastic processes {''W''(''t''), t&nbsp;≥&nbsp;0} and {''Z''(''t''), t&nbsp;≥&nbsp;0} are said to solve the Skorokhod problem if for all non-negative ''t'' values,
# <math>W(t)=X(t)+R Z(t)\ge 0</math>
# <math>Z(0)=0</math> and <math>dZ(t) \ge 0</math>
# <math>\int_0^t W_i(s)\text{d}Z_i(s)=0</math>.

The matrix ''R'' is often known as the reflection matrix, ''W''(''t'') as the reflected process and ''Z''(''t'') as the regulator process.
